fullDescription: The fourth cohort of the HER WAKA series focuses on personal branding and career growth — treating your career like a Go-To-Market strategy.

Andrea Halal, Tech Marketing Leader at Ideqa and creator of Big Leap Energy, will share how she rebuilt her network and professional credibility after moving to New Zealand with no local connections. Drawing on nine years of marketing experience across TV, production, advertising, brand management, and B2B marketing, Andrea will walk participants through the practical steps for building visibility and trust when you are new, relocating, or pivoting.

Expect a grounded, strategy-driven session on using LinkedIn as a career tool (not a highlight reel), on why positioning matters as much as performance, and on how relationships quietly compound over time.
As with every HER WAKA cohort, RCSA will join the session to share insights on the current New Zealand job market and offer practical guidance on job-seeking.

HER WAKA is a dynamic, employment-focused programme delivered by SheSharp in Auckland for Ministry of Social Development clients who are ready to strengthen their pathway into work. Running monthly from March to June 2026, each session is a cohesive, repeatable event designed to build job readiness, confidence, and practical understanding of the New Zealand labour market.
NOTE: This event is strictly by invitation only.

speakers.name: Andrea Halal
speakers.title: Tech Marketing Leader | Building Your Career GTM Strategy
speakers.bio: Andrea Halal is a Tech Marketing Leader at Ideqa driving B2B growth across ANZ, and the creator of Big Leap Energy — a career Go-To-Market methodology for tech professionals building visibility, credibility, and networks from scratch. After relocating to New Zealand with no local connections, she applied marketing thinking to her own career and rebuilt from zero. She is Ambassador Lead and Operations Strategy at The Marketing Club AU/NZ, writes and speaks on personal branding, LinkedIn as a career tool, and the mindset of showing up before you feel ready.

speakers.title: Founder & Managing Director of BrightSpark
speakers.bio: With over 20 years’ experience in recruitment and 15 years in New Zealand’s tech and digital sector, Lisa brings deep expertise in hard-to-fill and specialist roles. She works closely with innovative companies and highly skilled candidates navigating competitive, short-market conditions. At the heart of Lisa’s work is helping people find roles that genuinely excite and fulfil them, while supporting businesses to thrive. A passionate advocate for people-first recruitment, Lisa runs jobseeker and graduate readiness workshops, champions Women in Tech, and supports inclusive hiring practices. She believes great recruitment can genuinely change lives.

She has a strong background in senior client management, candidate placement and career coaching, helping professionals build personal brands and sharpen their interview skills. Sri stands out for her ability to find talent for niche, high-impact roles such as product management and technical leadership, having recruited product owners, senior data architects and testers.

detailPageData.title: Making LinkedIn Work for You with Stuart Little, presented by She Sharp and AUT
detailPageData.subtitle: Presented by She Sharp and AUT (Engineering, Computer and Mathematical Sciences)
fullDescription: In today’s changing world of work, your LinkedIn® profile is more than a CV. It is your personal brand, your digital presence and often the first impression you make before a conversation even begins.
Opportunities are no longer only applied for — they are discovered. Recruiters, hiring managers and businesses are actively searching for people with the right skills, mindset and visibility.
How you show up on LinkedIn directly influences what finds you.

This session is led by Stuart Little, Creative Strategist and Director of Agency8. Through his work supporting professionals, businesses and large-scale programmes across New Zealand, Stuart brings a real-world perspective on how LinkedIn is actually being used today to identify, assess and connect with talent for a changed job market.

Rather than focusing on theory, this workshop draws on practical insight, current hiring trends and proven strategies that help people move from having a profile to building a presence that creates momentum.
You will gain a clearer understanding of how to position yourself, how to be found, and how to use LinkedIn as a tool that works for you consistently.

This session will provide the knowledge to build a LinkedIn® presence that reflects who you are, what you do, and how you work. The focus is not just on creating a profile, but on positioning yourself in a way that attracts the right opportunities and builds long-term career momentum.
This workshop is presented in partnership with She Sharp and AUT (Engineering, Computer and Mathematical Sciences) as part of New Zealand’s Digital Suite.

speakers.bio: Janelle Wright is the founder of Janelle's Recruitment. She helps professionals stand out and land the right roles through personal branding, ATS-optimised CVs, LinkedIn strategy, interview coaching and proactive recruitment. Her process works. 90% of candidates secure roles, she's built a strong industry network and her LinkedIn following has grown past 9,000. Janelle has worked and coached for major global brands around the world. She takes a people-first approach with real pace behind it, so candidates don't just find a job they build a career.

detailPageData.title: From Burnout to Balance

location.address: Level 13, PwC Tower, Commercial Bay, Auckland

fullDescription: Our “From Burnout to Balance” breakfast event is going to be an enlightening morning where we delve into two vital aspects of well-being. As women, we wear many hats - we are professionals, mothers, partners, and more. It is this dance of roles that showcases our adaptability, but also puts us at a greater risk of burnout. In addition, the boundaries between work and personal life are becoming increasingly blurred.

Our incredible speakers will guide you on a journey towards achieving equilibrium in the fast-paced world of technology, looking at actionable strategies to harmonise professional ambitions with self-care.

Brigette McGregor-Macdonald will speak to discovering the power of mindfulness and provide key techniques that empower you to stay centred, enhance focus, and build resilience against burnout.‍ Maja Lee will dive into the critical connection between nutrition, health and stress management, providing insights into putting your health first for peak performance, optimising energy levels and warding off burnout. It is time to invest in your well-being, embrace balance, and unlock your full potential in both your professional and personal life.
Join us as we change the narrative from ‘Burnout’ to ‘Balance’.

speakers.name: Brigette McGregor-Macdonald
speakers.title: Executive Coach and Faciliator
speakers.bio: Brigette is an Executive Coach and Facilitator who helps people cut through life's noise to achieve success. Based in Auckland Brigette has developed an extensive coaching toolkit over the last 20+ years working in the leadership and development field in London, Singapore and now back in New Zealand. Brigette uses curiosity, empathy and toolkit of resources to support people to grow, change and feel less ‘stuck’. Brigette works with people to articulate their vision vs reality and to build a roadmap to tackle challenges. She has a pragmatic business focus and a personal interest and practise in how mindfulness can support business success, resilience and to find more joy in life.

speakers.name: Maja Lee
speakers.title: Customer Performance Marketing Lead, Sky TV
speakers.bio: Maja is a mindful marketing leader, with a track record of driving marketing transformation for global and local brands. After the birth of her daughter, Valentina, Maja founded Foodie Babe, a baby food company focused on vegetables and spices, and she's on a mission to cultivate healthy and adventurous eaters. Currently leading the performance marketing team at Sky TV, Maja loves her work and thrives on connecting fans with top-notch sports and entertainment. She's dedicated to promoting a vibrant and healthy lifestyle, driven by her passion for nutrition, movement, and mindfulness.

speakers.name: Danubia Paim (Dani)
speakers.title: Founder, Property Besties
speakers.bio: Dani Paim bought her first property at 19 with no safety net — just determination and fear. Today she's the founder of Property Besties, New Zealand's most collaborative property investor community (100+ members), and Wealth & Wellness Co., helping women build financial independence without sacrificing what matters most. A former financial advisor, Dani saw women needed clarity, confidence and community — not more information. She left the 9–5 to create supportive, values-driven spaces. She's coached 200+ Kiwis and is on a mission to help 1,000 women invest in property while living fully now, not just at retirement.

speakers.name: Wyndi Tagi
speakers.title: Co-Founder WE Mana & The Table
speakers.bio: Wyndi Tagi is a business strategist, speaker, and community builder passionate about helping people live with purpose and lead with mana. After building and successfully exiting her accounting firm, she now supports purpose-driven founders to grow sustainable businesses without losing themselves in the process. As founder of The Table, a global community for culturally aligned business owners, Wyndi creates spaces where women belong, build, and become. She believes in the power of "Give To Gain" — that when women share wisdom, courage, and support, everyone rises.

speakers.name: Annette Rangi

With a career spanning roles as CTO, GM Operations, and Programme Manager across sectors including construction, retail, energy, and government, she champions agile leadership, innovation, and emerging technology adoption. A passionate advocate for diversity, Annette has coached and mentored teams of over 150 people and is experienced in Scaled/Lean-Agile, SAFe, SCRUM, and DevOps methodologies.

specialSections.title: Forming Your Team
content: Register as an individual and join a team on the first morning, or register with a team you have already formed — either works.

We recommend teams of three to six members. A hackathon is a safe space for people from different skill sets and backgrounds to gather around a problem, and a good mix — technical, design, domain and commercial — consistently produces stronger solutions.
Mentors are there from the start to help people find each other and to check that teams are the right size and balanced.
On day two, pitch practice starts around midday. Most teams split at this point — some keep building towards the solution, others start building the pitch.
The team comes back together for the 30 minutes between the end of the hack and the start of pitching.

specialSections.title: How Mentors Help You
content: Technical Experts — answer complex technical questions, sense-check your design and suggest alternatives, with deep expertise in AI and data. They will not build it for you, but they will show you where it is going wrong.
Subject Matter Experts — know the problem domain and can tell you whether your solution would genuinely work for the people it is meant to help.
Business Experts — check in often on team dynamics, problem framing and the story you are telling, and help you shape a pitch that lands in five minutes.
Mentors are available across both days. Ask early and ask often — that is what they are here for.

specialSections.title: How Teams Are Judged
content: Each venue has a panel of three to four judges: a host representative, a sponsor or business representative, and a member of the AI Forum Executive Council.
Each team delivers a live 5-minute pitch to the panel, followed by a short Q&A with the judges.
Judges score four equally-weighted criteria (1–5 each):
Inspiration — a clearly defined problem, a solution that solves it, and real impact for New Zealand and the world.
Technology — the solution must use AI; demonstrate feasibility, engineering quality, and how the technology solves the problem (a working prototype is highly recommended).
Design & Innovation — originality, user experience, and inventive use of technology.
Presentation — a clear, creative pitch that addresses the problem and answers judges' questions within the time limit.
Every venue in the festival scores against the same scorecard. The TAIAO scorecard weights all four categories equally; the Technical Brilliance scorecard is weighted towards Technology.
Every pitch is recorded. Each venue announces its own winner on the day, and that winning pitch goes forward to the national judging panel.
All judging panel decisions are final.
An optional pitch deck template is available in the Community Hub as a guide.

specialSections.title: What the Judges Look For
content: Judges have very little time to absorb an idea that may be completely unfamiliar to them. Judges from the last five years of the festival advise focusing on three things:
Does it solve an important UN Sustainable Development Goal problem?
Is the solution feasible and achievable?
Will it make an impact?
And for the Technical Brilliance prize, a fourth: does it demonstrate strong technical thinking?

specialSections.title: National Judging Panel
content: The national panel watches every venue's winning pitch video, scores it against the same scorecards used at each venue, and selects the one winner who pitches on stage at the Aotearoa AI Summit. The same panel awards the AI Technical Brilliance Prize, which can go to any venue winner — not only the national winner.

Albert Bifet (University of Waikato) chairs the panel and David Knox (Topologic) is deputy chair. They are joined by Prof Yun Sing Koh and Prof Karin Bryan (University of Auckland), Nicholas Fourie (Fisher & Paykel Healthcare), Dr Mahsa McCauley (AUT, Chair of AI Forum New Zealand), Dr Karaitiana Taiuru (AI, data and emerging technology ethics, governance and research; Chair of Kāhui Māori), Shivonne Llondt (AWS) and Nicola Voice (Sustainability Lead, Woolworths New Zealand).
Dr Mahsa McCauley and Nicholas Fourie sit on both the AUT City Campus venue panel and the national panel.

specialSections.title: Your 5-Minute Pitch, Section by Section
content: Connect — 30 seconds. Who are you and what is your passion? Think of it as speed dating: you get one first impression.

Problem to Solve — 1 minute. What problem are you solving, and why should anyone care? Who or what does it impact? Humanise it with a short story, and back it with data — this is an AI hack, after all.
Your Big Idea — 2 minutes. How does your innovation solve the problem, and how does it meet the brief? Show us your prototype — high-fidelity or click-through slideware is fine.
Future Impact — 1.5 minutes. What will your innovation change? What do you need to make it work? And what could it mean for the future?
Describe the problem you actually ended up solving — it is not always the one you set out to solve.

specialSections.title: Featured Problem — F&P Healthcare: Facilities Helpdesk Agent
content: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, a sponsor of the festival, has put forward a process optimisation challenge: design an AI agent for its Facilities Helpdesk — the single point of contact for maintenance and facilities service requests across the organisation.

Today the experience places unnecessary effort on both the people raising requests and the Facilities team. Intake, prioritisation, escalation guidance and status communication all rely on manual steps, separate process knowledge and email follow-up. The result is inconsistent processes that sit outside the tools staff use day to day, incomplete request data, no real-time visibility for the requestor, and sub-optimal escalation responses.

The opportunity is to create a more employee-friendly front door for Facilities requests: guiding staff through structured intake in plain language — in their own words — applying the existing priority process consistently, surfacing escalation guidance at the right moment, and keeping requestors informed throughout.

How it matches the UN Sustainable Development Goals: being inclusive means every employee can engage in their own language and has equal visibility of progress (SDGs 8, 9 and 10); removing wasted effort, resources and rework makes the process more sustainable (SDG 12); and F&P Healthcare's solutions support good health and well-being (SDG 3).

F&P frames this as "Care by Design" — good people doing good work with intent. When reviewing and judging pitches, F&P is looking for teams whose design is genuinely underpinned by that Culture of Care, and which centre people and process ahead of technology. specialSections.title: Featured Problem — F&P Healthcare: Restoration Intelligence
content: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, a sponsor of the festival, has put forward a second challenge — this one from its sustainability team: Restoration Intelligence, turning drone data into environmental insights. As part of developing F&P's new Karaka campus, the team is restoring the Oiroa Stream and surrounding wetlands, where employees, families and community members have planted more than 3,000 native plants across 22 species since 2023 to improve biodiversity, water quality, habitat connectivity and climate resilience.

Ecological restoration projects increasingly use drones to collect imagery and video, but measuring restoration outcomes still relies on specialist ecological and Geographic Information System (GIS) expertise. As a result, monitoring is often manual, expensive, infrequent and hard to scale, requiring extensive fieldwork in difficult terrain.

The challenge is to build an AI-powered restoration monitoring solution that automates the analysis of periodic drone imagery — annual surveys collected over the 20+ year lifetime of a landscape restoration project — along with drone video, to quantify ecological outcomes and generate actionable insights. Where available, it should integrate additional data such as biodiversity records, GIS layers and historical monitoring datasets, reducing reliance on manual assessment, specialist expertise and fragmented tools.

Teams are encouraged to address as many of the restoration monitoring metrics below as they choose — they do not need to tackle them all, since solutions may be limited by the availability of open-source data and tools. In the absence of drone images, large-scale restoration projects such as Matuku Link (Te Henga), Waikereru Ecosanctuary (Gisborne) and Hinewai Reserve (Akaroa) may offer suitable proxy and historical satellite imagery for training and testing.

How it matches the UN Sustainable Development Goals: the project supports SDG 15 – Life on Land through improved monitoring of biodiversity and restoration outcomes, and SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production through more efficient, better-informed stewardship of natural resources. It aligns with F&P Healthcare's values of Innovation and Life and its intention to create a positive, lasting impact on society and the environment.

specialSections.title: What to Measure — Restoration Metrics
content: Tree survival (%) — planting success and areas of plant mortality
Native species richness — biodiversity and diversity of the native plant community
Keystone species tracking (e.g. Kahikatea, Kauri, Pukatea) — establishment and survival of priority species
Natural regeneration density — self-seeded recovery and ecosystem self-sustainability
Native canopy cover (%) — vegetation establishment and habitat development
Exotic plant cover (%) and weed cover (%) — non-native competition and invasive pressure
Riparian shade cover (%) — stream shading that supports water quality and temperature
Time-series imagery and change detection — visual storytelling of restoration progress over time

specialSections.title: Featured Problem — My Life My Voice: Accessible UI Generation
content: My Life My Voice has submitted a featured problem on accessible user interface (UI) generation for developers. Millions of people with disabilities encounter barriers every day because the apps and digital tools they rely on were not built accessibly. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) exist precisely to address this — yet compliance rates remain persistently low.

The bottleneck is not developer intent; it is workflow. Accessibility checking is manual, happens late in the build process, and sits outside the tools developers actually use. When it does exist, it audits what is already broken rather than preventing the problem at the point of creation.

The opportunity is to create an AI-powered tool that embeds accessibility support directly into the development workflow — enabling developers to check UI components against WCAG criteria in real time, and to generate accessible layout options at the point of design rather than after the fact. Unlike existing checkers (such as Microsoft's accessibility tools), the focus here is on generative support: producing accessible options, not just flagging inaccessible ones.

Why AI, why now: current AI coding tools optimise for speed and functionality, and none meaningfully optimise for accessibility. An AI layer that understands accessibility standards could shift accessibility from an audit task to a design default — making inclusive UI the path of least resistance for any developer, regardless of their prior knowledge of disability or accessibility standards.

How it matches the UN Sustainable Development Goals: SDG 4 – Quality Education, SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth, and SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities. Designing user interfaces that cater to people of all abilities increases opportunities for education and economic contribution, and reduces barriers to access and therefore inequalities.

content: Disabled people who currently encounter inaccessible digital products daily
Developers who want to build inclusively but lack embedded, standards-based support to do so
Businesses and app developers losing disabled customers — and their revenue — because their products cannot be accessed
Organisations navigating increasing legal and regulatory pressure around digital accessibility

infoSections.title: About the Venue
paragraphs: The event is hosted in person at AUT City Campus, 55 Wellesley Street East, in the heart of Auckland's CBD — well served by public transport and within walking distance of the city centre. Look for the Sir Paul Reeves Building, known on campus as the WG Building.

Registration and all catering are in WG306, the foyer area, on both days. WG308 — the Wave Room — is the main room: the opening on Friday evening, and the pitches and awards on Saturday. Please allow time to find parking and sign in before 5:00pm on Friday.

Teams also get rooms of their own to work in. On Friday those are WG128, WG128A, WG129 and WG100D. On Saturday the working spaces move and open out: the lecture theatres WG403 and WG404, and the classrooms WG607–WG609, WG701–WG703, WG801–WG803 and WG808. The mentors are based in WG809 on Saturday — that is where to find them if nobody is roaming past your table.
Please bring your laptop and charger, a reusable water bottle, and a notebook and pen if you like working on paper. Power, Wi-Fi, mentoring, and food and drinks are provided on site across both days.

Our hosts are welcoming you into their space, so please follow their guidance and rules. Participants who choose not to abide by these rules may be asked to leave.

infoSections.title: Intellectual Property
paragraphs: Neither the AI Forum nor any supporter of this festival has any interest in the intellectual property created at the event. For practical purposes, any IP created belongs to the team that created it — your team may want to agree how that works going forward after the event.

Participants must comply with the terms and conditions of any intellectual property rights that already exist over anything they use during the hackathon. Any infringement of those rights is at the participant's own risk.

fullDescription: AI is changing the way we work — and it's no longer just a topic for technologists. Join She Sharp and Les Mills for an inspiring conversation about how AI is creating opportunities across every function, from technology and data to communications, legal, finance, and commercial leadership. Through a panel of cross-functional leaders driving AI transformation in their fields, we'll explore the practical realities of adopting AI, the mindset shifts required to embrace change, and the skills that will help people thrive in an AI-enabled future.

You'll hear perspectives from experts across technology, change management, commercial strategy, and legal, before joining interactive table discussions on how individuals and organisations can drive positive change with AI. Whether you're a developer, marketer, lawyer, analyst, people leader, or simply curious about where AI is heading, this event is designed to challenge the idea that AI belongs to one department. The future of work will be shaped by people from every background — and we believe AI is now everyone's job. Come ready to learn, connect, and be inspired by the many pathways into the next generation of careers.
